records.building: Footpath along Yuk Choi Road opposite to MN Wing
records.description: PolyU applies Eco-Block here. It is an environmentally friendly paving block which is made by a patented technology developed by PolyU. It effectively uses recycled glass and construction waste as major constituents in the production of concrete blocks to remove air pollutants, such as nitrogen oxides (NOx). It not only reduces the disposal of waste, but also conserves the use of natural resources, such as river sand.

records.address: QT005, G/F, Chow Yei Ching Building (QT)
records.description: Concrete is a commonly used building material in the Hong Kong construction industry. Equipped with facilities such as environmental curing chambers, high temperature furnaces, oxygen and chloride diffusion equipment for concrete permeability testing, and mercury intrusion porosimeters, the Concrete Technology Laboratory steers research in the area of advanced concrete technologies. It contributes to the development of environmentally friendly concrete products from recycled aggregates derived from construction and demolition wastes.

records.name: Indoor Air Quality (Bioaerosal) Laboratory
records.description: The Indoor Air Quality (Bioaerosal) Laboratory at Biological Safety Level 2 (BSL-2) is equipped with a Class II biological safety cabinet. Lab scientists and technicians have expertise in a wide variety of technical areas, such as bacterial growth analysis and experimental synthesis, field and environmental sampling, influence of ventilation on airborne microorganism dispersal and deposition, etc. The lab is also equipped with a wide range of advanced bioaerosol sampling facilities for laboratory and field studies.

records.name: Indoor Environmental Quality (IEQ) Laboratory
records.description: The Indoor Environmental Quality (IEQ) Laboratory facilitates teaching, research and consultancy projects that focuses on evaluating the environmental conditions found inside buildings. A wide spectrum of instruments, equipment and test facilities have been acquired, with portable test rigs to help in the evaluation of thermal comfort, indoor air quality and ventilation performance.

records.building: Ho Iu Kwong Building/ Industrial Centre (W)
records.description: The Industrial Centre (IC) is a 'Technical Library' equipped with a complete collection of engineering facilities, equipment and technologies for staff and students to realize their research and project activities. It is the only establishment of its kind among the local 8 UGC-funded universities. It provides a multi-disciplinary open environment where students can integrate their skills and knowledge for real life problems through hands-on learning activities. It also supports a lot of the University's research projects and knowledge transfer activities.

records.name: Intelligent Building Laboratory
records.description: The Intelligent Building (IB) Laboratory provides state-of-the-art test facilities for R&D on Intelligent Building technologies, advanced building system control, building management systems and building automation. This lab embraces the latest energy-efficient building management solutions including cloud-based integrated building management systems to facilitate effective teaching and learning and support innovative building solutions for local professionals.

records.name: Low-carbon Building Technology Laboratory
records.description: The Low-carbon Building Technology Laboratory consists of a stainless-steel cladded environmental chamber of a typical office size, and a stand-alone air-conditioning system, instrumented with three thermal manikins, temperature, aerosol, and VOC sensors. It accommodates a variety of experimental studies.

records.name: Material Resource Centre
records.description: The Material Resource Centre (MRC) is a place showcasing materials representing current trends in design, materials research and productions globally. It contains thousands of material samples (including those of recycling and upcycling in nature), Pantone colour libraries and collections of local materials from manufacturers and suppliers. Every material sample is linked to a database containing all the related detailed descriptions and information, including contacts of manufacturers and distributors. The Centre is open to all PolyU staff, students and alumni.

records.name: Ng Wing Hong Laboratory for Sustainable City
records.description: The Ng Wing Hong Laboratory for Sustainable City aims to create a high-level information technology infrastructure for examining the sustainable development of Hong Kong at the building and city level. It facilitates the effective use of GIS and BIM techniques in urban sustainability, urban development, construction and other relevant disciplines. Equipped with rich multimedia facilities, it supports teaching and research, and provides a space for interacting with external stakeholders to address complex issues faced in the built environment.

It is the hub of a comprehensive range of facilities and equipment, and it organizes regular workshops and conferences to foster positive exchange among research institutions and industry players.

records.name: Public Design Lab
records.description: PolyU's Public Design Lab was established in 2007 and is the pioneering lab of its kind in the world. It is set up with a mission to promote public design in order to serve new and changing urban needs. Its focus is on public furniture and facilities to serve the public and to fit into the public environment. It runs numerous successful projects including the innovative UniRe(c), toilets that meet the needs of the blind, and bollards for urban areas.

records.name: Renewable Energy Lab
records.description: Established in August 2014, the Renewable Energy Laboratory enables fundamental and applied research on solar energy materials and green building materials in collaboration with industry and leading academic institutions, providing advanced and innovative technological solutions for the generation of renewable energy and a sustainable built environment.

records.name: Solar Simulation Laboratory
records.description: The Solar Simulation Laboratory provides facilities for testing solar energy devices for thermal and photovoltaic applications. The solar simulator is mainly used for the research and development of solar energy applications in buildings, product tests of solar energy equipment and heat loss measurements of various building facade elements and devices. Other renewable energy test rigs are also available in the lab.

records.name: Sustainability Management Research Centre
records.description: Sustainability Management Research Centre (SMRC) is a platform to pool the research strengths of the Faculty of Business and its external research partners in order to perform innovative research on sustainability management in collaborative efforts. It aspires to be a leading force in sustainability research and application. It is multi-disciplinary in nature, aiming at promoting corporate social responsibility as a model for achieving economic, social and environmental sustainability through management innovation.

records.name: Photovoltaic Solar Covered Walkway
records.address: P/F, Suen Chi Sun Memorial Square
records.description: PolyU supports energy conservation at the highest levels and encourages renewable energy utilization. High-efficiency Copper Indium Gallium Diselenide (CIGS) thin-film solar cells have been installed on the rooftop of the covered walkway on the Podium to effectively convert solar energy into electricity. The output of CIGS solar cells on a clear sunny day provides enough electricity to run 340 walkway lights and saves up to 10 tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalents greenhouse gas emissions annually. This is equivalent to the planting of 400 trees of at least 5 meters each in height.

records.name: Solar Photovoltaic System
records.description: PolyU supports energy conservation at the highest levels and encourages renewable energy utilization. A solar photovoltaic system was installed on the roof of Lee Shau Kee Building (Block Y) to provide energy for the building in 2006. The system consists of 126 solar panels of 175 Wp mono-crystalline silicon, with 3 kW grid tie inverters were used for a grid-connected Building-Integrated Photovoltaic (BIPV) application to generate about 20,000 to 25,000 kWh of electricity each year, depending on the rate of annual solar radiation. The amount of electricity generated is equivalent to about saving HK$20,000 per year of expense on electricity purchase.
